title: React.memo and useMemo Strategy
statement:
Optimize a slow list component using React.memo and useMemo. This challenge teaches you how to identify and fix unnecessary re-renders, which is critical for application performance.

Your task:
1. Identify which components are re-rendering unnecessarily
2. Apply React.memo to prevent re-renders of non-changing props
3. Use useMemo to memoize expensive computations
4. Use useCallback to maintain stable function references
5. Measure and compare performance before/after optimization
constraints: Must not wrap everything in React.memo indiscriminately
useMemo and useCallback should only be used where justified
Dependencies arrays must be correct (no infinite loops or stale values)
Must maintain exact same functionality before and after
complexity: Time: O(n) for rendering, O(1) for memoized computations, Space: O(n) for memoization cache
commonMistakes: Using React.memo on every component without measuring first
Missing dependencies in useMemo/useCallback causing stale values
Including too many dependencies causing constant recomputation
Not using useCallback with React.memo children (defeats the purpose)
Creating new object/function props inside render without memoization
Assuming React.memo alone solves performance issues
